hypotheses.statement: In at least one version an element painted above the price note (an overlay, sticky/positioned block or veil) hides the text even though the text itself has opacity 1 and visibility visible. d1 recorded isCovered true on one version and false on the other at both viewports with identical rects, but only from stack[0] background alpha, so this is not established.
hypotheses.prediction: At points inside the text rect, the version with the symptom shows one or more entries above the target whose backgroundColor alpha x opacity is high, and its text-rect pixels are nearly uniform (p05 close to p50, close to the reference clip); the other version shows no such entries and dark ink (low p05) distinct from the reference.
hypotheses.falsifier: No entry above the target with non-trivial alpha on either version, or text-rect pixels showing clear ink (p05 well below the reference clip's p05) on the version that has such entries.

hypotheses.statement: In at least one version the text is drawn but with a colour too close to its background (own colour, own background, or an ancestor filter/blend/opacity reducing ink), so it is present in the DOM and not covered but cannot be read.
hypotheses.prediction: That version's target style.color is close to the background colour or an ancestor lists a filter/blend/opacity; its text-rect pixels show p05 near the reference clip's p05 and histogram16 mass concentrated in the top bins, with no strong overlay above the target.
hypotheses.falsifier: Both versions report dark text colour on light background, no non-default ancestor filter/blend/opacity, and text-rect p05 far below the reference clip on both.

hypotheses.statement: The text users should see is a different instance or position than the one d1 measured (d1 read only the first of up to N matches): e.g. a duplicate copy, a clipped/zero-size or off-viewport instance, while the measured one differs between versions only incidentally.
hypotheses.prediction: findText returns more than one match on at least one version, or matches differ between versions in rect/inViewport/display; pixel and stack measurements differ between matches within a version.
hypotheses.falsifier: Exactly one match per version with the same rect and in-viewport state on both versions, so the difference must lie in painting or covering of that single element.

probe.question: For every findText match of the affected text on each version and viewport: what is painted above it at sample points inside its rect (all stack entries above the target, with parsed alpha x opacity), what are its own colours and non-default ancestors, and how do the rendered greyscale pixels inside its rect compare with a same-size background reference clip?
probe.falsifier: If both versions give the same stacks above the target, the same own colours/ancestors and statistically similar text-rect vs reference pixel statistics at both viewports, none of the three hypotheses separates the versions and d1's isCovered split is unexplained by these measurements.
controls: Same-size reference clip just below (or above) the text rect, pixel statistics for plain background
One elementsFromPoint control point at the centre of the reference clip, to see whether any overlay also covers non-text background
Identical code, points and clips on both versions and both viewports; no branch on packet.target
limitations: elementsFromPoint stacks are capped at 8 and omit pseudo-elements; a ::before/::after overlay will not appear as an entry
The reference clip may contain other content (e.g. neighbouring text) rather than pure background
Matches outside the viewport are only partially measured (clips clamped; no scrolling)
Target identification in a stack uses tag+cls+rect, then text; if not found the whole stack is reported with targetIndex -1
Greyscale pixels do not capture hue contrast
Only stack[...] backgroundColor and opacity are known for overlying entries, not their filters or images

revisionNote: From d1 per critic: findText max 5 and every match measured; elementsFromPoint at 15 integer points inside each visible rect plus one reference point, every entry above the target (or whole stack if target absent) returned compactly with parsed rgb/rgba alpha x opacity, deduplicated stacks; own color/backgroundColor/fontSize/fontWeight/position/zIndex and nonDefaultAncestors (filter, blend, opacity) returned raw; pixels on the text rect (clamped, width<=800, height<=300) and a same-size reference clip with min/p01/p05/p50/max/below/histogram16 and artifact; viewport screenshot always taken; every call guarded so missing fields, empty stacks or zero matches still complete; no verdict booleans.
